question: Do the two measured guards (two_layer adoption gate, 0.75 adoption floor) keep the reorder pass's interleave-class gains while eliminating the v6.0 damage?
answer: Yes, decisively on the sequence lens: v6.1 mean 0.9075 versus the v5 champion side's 0.8595 - the campaign's first mean above 0.90 - with exactly three adoptions, all two-layer, all final sequence >= 0.82, the trio swept (0.2979 to 0.8237, 0.3758 to 0.7636, 0.7772 to 0.8679), zero single-layer adoptions, and non-adopted pages slightly better than baseline (0.9202 vs 0.9132). The judged lens paid a localized price: -0.3pt overall (0.9722 vs 0.9751), entirely the three reordered pages (-3.1 to -4.0pt each, all still 0.90-0.94), while non-reordered pages improved on both lenses.

decision: adopted as development champion; judged gate recorded as marginally failed
decision_detail: v6.1 is the first candidate whose sequence mean crosses 0.90, its guards behaved exactly as measured evidence predicted, and its only cost is a localized -3 to -4pt judged dip on the three pages whose reading order improved by +9 to +53 points - pages the printed edition previously could not render in order at all. Non-reordered pages improved on both lenses, so the champion swap strictly dominates outside the trio and trades judge-prose coherence for structural reading order inside it. Follow-up named: fragment-placement smoothing (leftover attachment produces mid-column shards the judge reads as noise) to recover the judged dip; the mth1000-006 session-order lottery remains the reliability residue (three measurements: 0.6059, 0.53, 0.60) with repeat-and-reconcile as its instrument.
next_permitted_action: v6.1 is the comparison baseline for the toolbelt7 autonomy harness; design fragment smoothing and the classifier-training preflight as parallel bounded experiments.
